title: Forgetting to Move Ball Marker Back
question: A player moves their ball marker one putter head to the side to avoid another player's line on the putting green. They forget to move the marker back, replace their ball at the wrong spot and hole the putt. What is the correct ruling in stroke play?

choices.text: The holed putt counts, and the player must add two penalty strokes. No replay is required.
The holed putt does not count, and the player must replay the putt from the correct spot with no penalty.
The holed putt counts, but the player is disqualified for playing from a wrong place.
The player adds two penalty strokes and must replay the putt from the correct spot.

explanation: When a player forgets to move their ball marker back to its original position on the putting green and holes out from the wrong spot, the holed putt counts, and the player receives the general penalty (two strokes in stroke play). There is no requirement to replay the putt because the ball was only a few inches from its correct place, so it is rarely a serious breach.

juniorVersion.title: Forgetting to Put Marker Back in the Right Spot
juniorVersion.question: On the green, you move your ball marker to the side so you don't block your friend's putt. You forgot to move your marker back and put your ball in the wrong place. You putt from there and get your ball in the hole. What happens now?

choices.text: Your ball in the hole counts, but you must add two extra shots. You do not have to putt again.
Your putt does not count, and you have to try the putt again from the right place. No extra shots.
Your putt counts, but you are out of the game for playing from the wrong place.
You must add two extra shots and try the putt again from the right place.

juniorVersion.explanation: Because you putted from the wrong spot, your putt counts, but you get two extra shots added to your score. You do not have to putt again because your ball was close to the right place.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A small thing (like a coin or disc) that shows where your ball was on the green.
The short grass around the hole where you use your putter.
In this case, it means two shots added to your score.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Remind children to always move their marker back before putting so their score does not get extra shots.
likelyMisconceptions: Some kids might think they have to putt again if they play from the wrong place, but if the ball was just a little bit away, the shot counts with two extra shots.
Kids might think they are out of the game for this mistake, but they just add two shots.
